issues.legal_issue: A later policy permitting a house-owning government employee to retain assigned accommodation on payment of rent obligations does not extinguish the employee’s right to seek possession of the employee’s own rented residence under the special eviction procedure when an earlier or continuing order requires the employee to vacate or incur obligations.
material_facts: The landlord owned the residence occupied by the tenants and occupied residential accommodation allotted to him as a government employee.

A general government order required employees who owned residences at their place of posting to vacate allotted accommodation or incur obligations, and a specific order also required the landlord to vacate or pay market rent.

A later government memorandum permitted house-owning employees to continue in allotted accommodation subject to rent obligations, including payment of full market rent where the income from their own house exceeded the prescribed threshold.
Nothing in the record showed that the earlier obligation to vacate or incur obligations, or the specific order, had been withdrawn.
The tenants argued that the later memorandum meant the landlord no longer had to vacate and could not use the special eviction procedure.
issues.conclusion: The later memorandum did not remove the landlord’s obligation or the resulting right to seek possession; it gave him the option to remain in government accommodation subject to rent obligations. The tenants could not compel him to exercise that option. The landlord was entitled to use the special eviction procedure, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14A(1) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 gives a landlord occupying residential accommodation allotted by the Central Government or a local authority a right to recover possession where a general or special order requires the landlord to vacate that accommodation or, in default, incur obligations because the landlord owns residential accommodation in the territory. Read with section 25B, the later government memorandum modified the financial terms for continued occupation but did not withdraw the earlier obligation; the landlord could elect to remain subject to those terms. Busching Schmitz Private Ltd. v. P.T. Menghani and Anr. was referred to for the principle that the cause of action includes the order to vacate and the resulting urgency to recover the landlord’s own building. K.D. Singh v. Shri Hari Babu Kanwal was overruled, and J.L. Paul v. Ranjit Singh was approved.

rule.if: special_eviction_appeal and landlord_owns_local_residence and landlord_occupies_assigned_government_residence and government_order_requires_vacating_or_incurring_obligations and later_policy_allows_retention_only_subject_to_rent_obligations and earlier_obligation_not_withdrawn

predicates.special_eviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a landlord’s use of a special eviction procedure for recovery of a rented residence.
predicates.landlord_owns_local_residence: The landlord owns a residence in the area where the landlord is posted or otherwise assigned accommodation.
predicates.landlord_occupies_assigned_government_re: The landlord occupies residential accommodation allotted by the government or a public authority.
predicates.government_order_requires_vacating_or_in: A general or specific government order requires the landlord to vacate the allotted accommodation or incur obligations because the landlord owns a local residence.
predicates.later_policy_allows_retention_only_subje: A later policy permits the landlord to remain in the allotted accommodation only subject to rent or other financial obligations.
predicates.earlier_obligation_not_withdrawn: No later order or other evidence shows that the obligation to vacate or incur obligations was withdrawn.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns the special eviction procedure and the landlord owns a local residence while occupying allotted government accommodation subject to an unwithdrawn vacate-or-pay obligation, a later policy allowing retention only on rent terms does not prevent the landlord from recovering possession through that procedure.
